name: field-service
description: The advanced demo: a multi-tenant field-service dispatch backend — shared region reference data, per-tenant customers, per-tenant work orders that move through a guarded life cycle, and the technicians' booked visits — with gapless job numbers, an SLA timer, integrity the database enforces, and a completion webhook to billing. Every construct here exists so one end-to-end test can measure one behaviour — see README.md for the construct-to-behaviour table.

work-order-ref.description: The letters WO, a dash, then four to eight digits. Written without ^...$ on purpose: Alvo anchors a format over the whole value, so a value with trailing text is refused by the framework's anchoring rather than by the author's.

billing.description: The billing system. In the demo stack a WireMock sidecar shares the Alvo container's network namespace, so localhost:9090 is loopback and the webhook egress guard admits it. Anywhere nothing listens there, a delivery to it fails and retries visibly on Operations — which is why only purchase-order jobs are sent (see the automation rule).

job-completed-to-billing.description: Tells billing a purchase-order job is done, once per completion, as its own retried delivery after the commit. A job without a purchase order is settled on site and never reaches billing.

regions.description: A service region. Shared reference data (a ciselnik): global rather than tenant-scoped, so every tenant reads the same rows.

code.description: The region's short code, unique across the instance.

customers.description: A customer of one tenant. Deliberately NOT audited, so its rows carry no version: no ETag is minted for one and an If-Match naming a version is refused rather than ignored.

tier.description: Which service tier the customer is on.

service_opens_hour.description: The hour (0-23, the tenant's local time) from which a technician may be on site. Empty = no restriction. The embedded host's before-write hook schedules against it.

service_closes_hour.description: The hour (1-24) by which a visit must end; after service_opens_hour when both are set.

work_orders.description: One job to be carried out for a customer, in a region, by a technician. Audited, so every row carries a version and every write of one can be made conditional.

reference.description: The human-facing work-order reference, unique within the instance.

description.description: The full job description as the customer gave it.

status.description: Where the job is in its life cycle. Every move is guarded by the state machine below: new, then scheduled, in progress and completed — or cancelled, and only an administrator reopens.

priority.description: Dispatch priority, 1 (highest) to 5 (lowest). Required, so a paged read may sort by it.

quoted_price.description: What the customer was quoted, excluding tax.

is_emergency.description: Whether the job was raised as an emergency call-out.

scheduled_for.description: When the technician is due on site. Nullable, so a paged read may NOT sort by it.

completed_on.description: The day the job was signed off, if it has been.

contact_email.description: Who to tell when the job is done.

metadata.description: Whatever the dispatch system attached to the job.

assigned_to.description: The user id of the technician the job is assigned to. The rules below compare it with @user.id, which is what makes a technician's list a subset rather than a refusal.

external_ref.description: The identifier this job carries in the customer's own system. Maintained by the integration, never by an API caller.

internal_notes.description: Dispatcher-only commentary. Confidential: neither the value nor the fact that this field exists may reach a caller, so it appears in no response and in no published schema.

access_code.description: The site access code the caller must supply on create and can never read back. Required AND hidden, which is the one case a hidden field's name is published — in the write schemas only.

customer_id.description: The customer this job is for.

region_id.description: The region the job is carried out in.

job_number.description: The gapless job number billing and the customer quote, assigned by Alvo on create, counted per tenant and per calendar year in Bratislava. Read-only: a write that sends it is refused.

respond_by.description: When an emergency must be scheduled by, from the customer's contract. Arms the sla_breach timer.

po_number.description: The customer's purchase order. One open job per customer and PO; a cancelled job releases it. A job on a PO is invoiced by billing when it is completed.

on_site_minutes.description: Minutes on site across the job's visits — what billing invoices. Maintained by Alvo.

schedule.description: A dispatcher books a technician and a time.

cancel.description: The customer or the desk calls it off, even mid-visit.

reopen.description: Only an administrator reopens a closed job.

sla_breach.description: An emergency still unscheduled at respond_by escalates.

visits.description: A technician's booked slot on a job: the dispatch calendar. Seen by a technician through the job it belongs to.

work_order_id.description: The job this visit is for.

technician_id.description: The user id of the technician booked.

minutes_on_site.description: Minutes actually spent, recorded at sign-off.

notes.description: What the technician wants the desk to know.

checks.message: A visit can only be booked on an open work order.
